purpose: How can two equal compass circles find the midway line?
meaning: A perpendicular bisector passes through a segment midpoint at a right angle. Two distinct intersections of equal-radius circles centered at the endpoints lie on this line. If the endpoint distance is d and circle radius is r, each intersection is h=√(r²−d²/4) above or below the segment. The intersection separation is ℓ=2 h.

definition.setting: A gardener wants a straight border equally distant from two stakes. Set their separation d and draw equal-radius compass circles around them. Their two intersections can be joined by a straightedge. Increase the compass radius and watch those points move apart while the midpoint line stays in the same place.

signature.d: Distance between the two stakes in metres
signature.h: Nonnegative intersection height above the stake line, in metres
signature.ℓ: Distance between the upper and lower intersections in metres; zero when the two coalesce at tangency

conditions: Both stake separation d and compass radius r range from 2 to 4 metres. Thus r≥d/2. At the only equality boundary d=4 m,r=2 m the circles touch once; for all other allowed inputs there are two intersections.
definition.domain_notes: This is an equal-radius rigid-compass construction. A tangent point is one point, not a pair that determines a line. The perpendicular bisector exists at tangency, but the two-intersection procedure cannot construct it there. Nonintersecting circles, arbitrary ruler constructions and the full classical construction theory remain separate.
